You are a software development instructor tasked with creating an educational module for beginner programmers who are learning Ruby, specifically focusing on the concept and application of classes in object-oriented programming. The module aims to demystify the concept of classes, illustrating how they serve as blueprints for objects, encapsulate data, and define methods for interacting with that data. A challenge has arisen because many students have expressed confusion over the syntax and practical use of classes, leading to difficulties in applying these concepts to real-world programming tasks. Your objective is to create a comprehensive learning module that addresses these issues, enhancing students' understanding and ability to effectively use classes in their programming projects.

The actions defined in this domain include:
    explain <class concept> <module content>: This action involves creating module content that clearly explains the concept of a class in Ruby, including its role as a blueprint for objects, how it encapsulates data, and how methods defined within a class interact with that data. The precondition for this action is that the instructor has a deep understanding of object-oriented programming principles and Ruby syntax. The effect of this action is a foundational knowledge that students can build upon as they learn more advanced programming concepts.

    demonstrate <class syntax and usage> <practical examples>: After explaining the concept of a class, this action involves providing practical, hands-on examples that demonstrate how to define a class in Ruby, how to create instances of that class, and how to define and call methods within a class. The precondition for this action is the availability of a programming environment where students can write and execute Ruby code. The effect of this action is that students gain practical experience and confidence in using classes in their own programming projects.

    facilitate <interactive coding exercises> <student engagement>: With the foundational knowledge and practical examples provided, this action involves students participating in interactive coding exercises that challenge them to define their own classes, create objects, and interact with those objects through methods. The preconditions for this action are that students have access to a programming environment and are willing to actively participate. The effect of this action is that students apply what they have learned in a hands-on manner, reinforcing their understanding and ability to use classes in Ruby effectively.

Your mission is to implement these strategies in the educational module, ensuring that students leave with a solid understanding of how to use classes in Ruby to structure their programs efficiently. This task requires a deep understanding of object-oriented programming, Ruby syntax, and the ability to create an engaging and educational learning environment.

  (:requirements :strips)
  (:predicates
    (has-deep-understanding ?instructor)
    (programming-environment-available)
    (students-willing-to-participate)
    (foundational-knowledge-acquired)
    (practical-experience-gained)
    (hands-on-understanding-reinforced)
  )

    :precondition (has-deep-understanding ?instructor)
    :effect (foundational-knowledge-acquired)
  )

    :parameters (?syntax_usage ?practical_examples)
    :precondition (programming-environment-available)
    :effect (practical-experience-gained)
  )

    :precondition (and (students-willing-to-participate) (programming-environment-available))
